question.text: As per the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 cited in the chapter, 'Retail Individual Investor' means an individual who applies or bids for specified securities up to a value of not more than:

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter quotes SEBI ICDR Regulations 2018: 'Retail individual investor' means an individual investor who applies or bids for specified securities for a value of not more than INR 2 lakh. This is the standard IPO retail threshold used by lead managers in the RII category. The Trap: (A) INR 1 lakh was an older threshold, raised to INR 2 lakh. (B) INR 10 lakh is the Specialized Investment Fund (SIF) minimum introduced by SEBI (Mutual Funds) Third Amendment 2024 — a different threshold entirely. (C) INR 5 lakh is not a regulatory threshold in this context. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) and XXI-A (PMS Distributor) test the retail/HNI/institutional thresholds together. III-A (Compliance) covers ICDR categorisation. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat I/II AIF minimum commitment is INR 1 crore (SEBI AIF Regs), so AIF LPs never fall in the RII bracket. But Managers running feeder structures via PMS/MFs need to remember the INR 2 lakh RII cut — relevant if the AIF runs a down-stream public-issue participation.
